items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Like you know the Gershwin tunes and Cole Porter and Jerome Kern and all that.

ctx.x: Maybe get the bench to move or something. Yeah. Well that was really enjoyable. And can I take you guys back a little bit to why this kind of music? Why did you get into jazz and swing music?

That’s really hard to say. I grew up in, I was born in 1929. So I grew up during the big band era, and like pop music was, a lot of it was standards. Like you know the Gershwin tunes and Cole Porter and Jerome Kern and all that. And a lot of it was “The Three Little Fishes.”
Well Mel Powell says he grew up when popular music was good and good music was popular.
